failedTasks.rationale: Pre-existing test failures in @reading-advantage/auth that were masked by the turbo cache in attempts 1-3 and exposed in attempts 4-6 when the auth package.json change (adding @types/bcryptjs in commit 73e38bc1) invalidated the auth#test cache, causing the full test suite to re-run. The suite has 21 pre-existing failing tests: (a) 9 integration tests in audit-retention*.integration.test.ts fail because DIRECT_DATABASE_URL is not set in the aggregate-gate environment (they need a real PostgreSQL database with a session-mode connection); (b) 2 quality-gate tests in phase-6-quality-gates.test.ts reference the archived track's plan.md at the old tracks/ path (the track was moved to archive/ in dec93670); (c) 1 stale dist/__tests__/token.test.js build artifact from the archived auth_security_hardening_20260611 track — the dist/token.js and dist/__tests__/token.test.js were left behind when the source token.ts was removed, and the auth package's pnpm test command (which has no vitest.config.ts to exclude dist/) picks up the stale artifact, which fails with `Cannot find package 'jsonwebtoken'`; (d) 9 duplicate dist tests are the compiled versions of the src/ integration + quality-gate tests, also picked up by vitest because the auth package has no vitest.config.ts. None of these failures is introduced by the ai_sdk_major_migration track. The migration-scope @reading-advantage/ai test suite (179 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed) is fully green. Fixing these auth#test failures would require either (i) modifying another track's test file (which violates the JR brief's 'preserve valid work; do not modify other tracks' tests' rule), (ii) setting up a real PostgreSQL database in the aggregate-gate environment (which is out of scope for the AI SDK migration), (iii) cleaning up the stale dist/ build artifacts (which is owned by auth_security_hardening_20260611), or (iv) adding a vitest.config.ts to the auth package that excludes dist/ (which is a build-config change to a different package and out of scope for the AI SDK migration).
